---
title: "Summary · Compose a Pico"
---

## Key takeaways

- **Declarative composition** of a Pico means binding each entry of
  its `spec.capabilities` to exactly one installed capsule whose
  `spec.capability` matches the identifier and whose
  `metadata.version` satisfies the stated constraint. The required
  Pico field set in
  [`definitions/pico.yaml`](../../../../definitions/pico.yaml) does
  not change (memo2 §3 D3 §2 amendment).
- **Two course terms, kept separate** (memo2 §4 D4):
  - **Rule compilation** = `bin/pico compose` in this repository,
    verified in [`memo24.md`](../../../../memo24.md) §2.4 as a
    Rule → artefact code generator. Not a capability composer.
  - **Capability composition / resolution** = the new operation
    defined in memo2 §4 D4. Normative semantics live in
    `open-engineering-capsules/source`; the reference CLI lives in
    `open-engineering-capsule/source`.
- **Three version constraints** (memo2 §2 D2): **bare** (any),
  **caret** `@X.Y.Z` (same major, version ≥ requested; `0.x` requires
  same minor and patch ≥ requested), **exact** `@=X.Y.Z` (strict
  equality). Every `metadata.version` MUST be
  [SemVer 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
- **Three v0.1 outcomes** (memo2 §1 D1, §3 D3 §2 amendment):
  `resolved` (exactly one surviving provider),
  `error: no-matching-provider` (zero survivors), and
  `error: multiple-matching-providers` (two or more survivors).
  Explicit provider selection is reserved for v0.2 via an
  upstream-owned `spec.composition` block; v0.1 Picos SHOULD NOT
  declare it.
- **Capability identifiers follow a fixed grammar** (memo2 §3 D3):
  two or more dot-separated lower-case segments; conforming examples
  `oe.greeting`, `github.issue.create`, `pico.state.set`; the
  authoritative home of the grammar will move to
  `open-engineering-conventions/pico-conventions/capability.schema.json`
  once committed (memo2 §5 follow-up (c)).
- **The Academy ships no resolver.** The lesson teaches hand
  resolution against the ten upstream scenarios and the
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/)
  Step 7 report. When the reference validator ships
  (memo2 §5 follow-up (b)), the Academy MAY add a thin delegating
  `pico resolve` wrapper that calls it — no local re-implementation
  (memo2 §4 D4).

## Three dependency-management rules this lesson exercises

From [`memo23.md`](../../../../memo23.md) §5:

- **Rule 3 — Explicit dependencies.** `spec.capabilities` declares,
  by capability identifier, exactly what a Pico needs; nothing is
  implicit or transitive.
- **Rule 6 — Compatibility checks.** The caret / exact / bare / `0.x`
  rules of memo2 §2 D2 are the contract-level compatibility check at
  v0.1; the breaking-change table in memo2 §2 D2 governs when a new
  capsule version requires a major bump.
- **Rule 7 — Reproducibility.** `@=X.Y.Z` (exact) is the
  "pin to this version" form used when reproducibility across
  environments matters more than tracking a line.

## What validates this today

| Check | Mechanism | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Capsule schema | Upstream `capsule.schema.json` fetched into `build/upstream/` | Lab Step 3 |
| Pico shape | `definitions/pico.yaml` → `spec.schema` via a Python one-liner | Lab Step 6 |
| Resolution | **By hand**, against the upstream scenarios; no Academy resolver (memo2 §5 follow-up (b) pending) | Lab Step 7, exercise Tasks A/B |
